demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian textile and apparel market anticipated to grow at a CAGR of 10%, reaching USD 350 billion by 2030, with exports contributing USD 100 billion.
- Domestic demand poised by increase in online retailing, shift from cotton to man-made fibre, fast fashion, and growth of the technical textiles segment.
- During FY 2025-26, exports of readymade garments and other textiles increased by about 10% over the previous year.
- Free trade agreements between India and UAE, Australia and Switzerland already in effect; agreements with UK and the European Union at final stage (FTA with UK finalized 6 May 2025), seen as supportive of export opportunities.
- Threats flagged: continuation of border tensions could impact economic projections; import duty of 10.6% continues, affecting India's price competitiveness; cheaper polyester yarn poses a price threat to cotton textiles in local innerwear markets.
- Revenue from operations resumed during FY 2025-26; the Company continues to focus on cost control, recovery and management of receivables, inventory discipline, reduction of financing burden and measured revival of operating activity.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company is pursuing a measured revival of its textile operations, including at Pali, Rajasthan, where it has started pilot operations. Future business expansion will be phased against actual demand, cash availability and operating performance, subject to timing and availability of working capital. Separately, the Board approved (07 September 2026) a Composite Scheme of Arrangement combining capital reduction/consolidation with a preferential issue of equity shares and warrants, intended to raise funds for repayment of borrowings/liabilities and for expansion, development and working-capital requirements of the Company's Pali textile business.
